messages.subject: [R-sig-Debian] getting started with rocker
messages.body_plain:
Dirk,

First time docker and rocker user here (and no programming expertise). After
trying on and off for several months, I managed to install and run rocker on my
Linux Mint, with RStudio running in the web browser
at?http://localhost:8787/?and I was finally able to figure out how to access
files, graphs, etc., that I save in RStudio at localhost:8787 by mounting a
folder from my host machine in the container, so files are saved on my system.?

A newbie question... Running this in the Linux terminal:

sudo docker run --rm -ti rocker/r-ver

starts the latest version of R, the 4 .6.0 (2026-04-24)

But running either:
sudo docker run --rm -ti -e PASSWORD=yourpassword -p 8787:8787 -v ~/rstudio-
projects:/home/rstudio rocker/tidyverse
or
sudo docker run --rm -ti -e PASSWORD=yourpassword -p 8787:8787 -v ~/rstudio-
projects:/home/rstudio rocker/rstudio

and then opening the localhost:8787, shows that it is running R version 4.4.1
(2024-06-14)

How do I update the R version in the rocker container?

Thank you for your help!
Luben

On 14 May 2026 at 10:35, Luben Dimov wrote:
| First time docker and rocker user here (and no programming expertise). After

| 
| A newbie question... Running this in the Linux terminal:
| 
| sudo docker run --rm -ti rocker/r-ver

Small aside: this is discouraged. You are generally better off making
yourself a member of the docker group so that you in your account can run
docker. Unconditionally letting docker run as root is somewhat dangerous.

See eg here https://docs.docker.com/engine/install/linux-postinstall/ or via
different tutorials.

|

| projects:/home/rstudio rocker/rstudio
| 
| and then opening the localhost:8787, shows that it is running R version 4.4.1
| (2024-06-14)
| 
| How do I update the R version in the rocker container?

Usually by downloading updated containers:  `docker pull rocker/rstudio`.

Cheers, Dirk

messages.subject: [R-sig-Debian] missing newer elpa-ess 24.01.1-5 package for Ubuntu 24.04 LTS?
messages.subject_clean: missing newer elpa-ess 24.01.1-5 package for Ubuntu 24.04 LTS?
messages.body_plain:
My machine running Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS uses the cloud.r-project.org
repository, as described in the instructions here:

  https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu/

That recently upgraded my r-base-core, which UNINSTALLED elpa-ess.
That's because the only available elpa-ess is version 24.01.1-1, which
r-base-core says is too old, via the "Breaks:" line shown below.

Is there a plan to make the newer elpa-ess available via the same
noble-cran40 repository r-base-core is coming from?  If not, is there
somewhere else we should get it from?

Currently, it looks like the official Ubuntu repositories have the
newer elpa-ess 24.01.1-5 available for Ubuntu 26.04 (resolute), but
only the older 24.01.1-1 is available for Ubuntu 24.04.4 (noble).
We can see that here:

  https://pkgs.org/search/?q=elpa-ess&on=name
  https://launchpad.net/ubuntu/+source/ess

My current workaround is simply to install ESS v25.01.0 from the
Github source.  (v26.01.0 doesn't seem to be tagged in Git.)
Fortunately this isn't hard, and so far seems to work fine:

  https://ess.r-project.org/index.php?Section=download
  https://github.com/emacs-ess/ESS


Output from my machine:
--------------------------------------------------
$ apt show r-base-core | egrep '^(Package|Version|Breaks):'
Package: r-base-core
Version: 4.6.0-4.2404.0
Breaks: elpa-ess (<< 24.01.1-5~), r-cran-gsl (<< 2.1-8-1+b1~), r-cran-rlang (<< 1.1.5-3~)

$ apt show elpa-ess | egrep '^(Package|Version|Breaks):'
Package: elpa-ess
Version: 24.01.1-1

$ grep DESCRIPTION /etc/lsb-release 
DISTRIB_DESCRIPTION="Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS"

$ grep '^deb' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/archive_uri-https_cloud_r-project_org_bin_linux_ubuntu-noble.list
deb https://cloud.r-project.org/bin/linux/ubuntu noble-cran40/
--------------------------------------------------

-- 
Andrew Piskorski <atp at piskorski.com>

Package maintainer here. That was because the elpa-ess package in its wisdom
decided to use what is known as 'autopkgtest', those failed, and it is
blocking passage of r-base from unstable to testing.

| Is there a plan to make the newer elpa-ess available via the same
| noble-cran40 repository r-base-core is coming from?  If not, is there
| somewhere else we should get it from?

Former ess package maintainer here: I just gave up on it as upstream made no
releases for years, and use elpa/melpa/... directly. I also orphaned the
package within Debian.  For a while we had another maintainer of ess /
elpa-ess in Debian but it looks like he stopped too.

Hth, Dirk
